item.title: Ubisoft CEO Offers Different Opinion On PlayStation Physical Discs Issue
item.description:
Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot weighed in on PlayStation's shift away from physical media during a recent earnings call, arguing that the decision "will not disturb the industry too much." The Ubisoft earnings call mostly addressed sales in the first quarter of the company's fiscal year, though Guillemot was also asked to address several different topics related to the company, as well as the industry as a whole.

At the beginning of July, PlayStation shared plans to phase out PS5 discs. The change won't take place until January 2028, at which point users will only be able to purchase games digitally. PlayStation attributed the decision to the changing habits of its users, noting that the majority of purchases made for PS5 games happen digitally.

Xbox Reportedly Testing Game-Changing Feature to Digitize Your Physical Games

Xbox plans for an all-digital future by apparently creating a way for fans to keep playing physical games purchased over the years.

By Marc Deschamps

Ubisoft CEO Compares Console Shift to PC Gaming

PlayStation's decision to move away from physical media has been likened to PC gaming, and Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot has made a similar comparison. Addressing a question about whether the move could prove to be positive or negative for the industry, Guillemot argued that "it helped to grow the market" when PC gaming went all-digital. Some analysts have noted that all-digital gaming could reduce costs, and the Ubisoft CEO seemed to echo that sentiment. Guillemot claimed that "there’s also some pressure for the future on the cost of machines, and being able to be only digital will help to have a more accessible machine."

Guillemot's opinion is significantly different from many others, as PlayStation's decision has resulted in strong backlash. Every post PlayStation makes on social media is quickly inundated with comments about the impending change, usually from frustrated PS5 owners. Even industry veterans open to the idea have shared the need for changes to the current model to make fans feel more comfortable with the concept of digital ownership. Former Blizzard president Mike Ybarra wants a "digital promise" from PlayStation, to ensure that games bought by users can't be taken away at a later date. Ybarra also argued for changes such as the ability to resell or lend out digital purchases.

It remains to be seen whether PlayStation will respond to the backlash and what impact it might have on the company's decision. Sony is facing an antitrust complaint in Mexico, where lawmakers argue that the PlayStation Store would become a monopoly as a result. The complaint also brings up how a lack of discs would hurt stores that specialize in selling used games, while limiting the options of consumers in areas without access to a stable internet connection.

As the backlash against PlayStation continues, it's likely that more figures in the video game industry will have opinions to share about the future of physical media. Some people are more optimistic than others about the decision by Sony, like Guillemot seems to be. However, it will be up to consumers to decide whether they want to continue to buy PlayStation products once they're only available digitally. A lot of fans are concerned about the future of ownership, and PlayStation has yet to offer plans that can help users feel confident about the future. Keeping PlayStation's most passionate fans invested is going to be important, especially as Sony begins shifting its internal resources towards the PS6.

Source: VGC

item.title: Monopoly GO: Free Dice Roll Links (Updated Daily)
item.description:
Monopoly GO is a fun board game that combines the classic Monopoly experience with cool additional features and a city-building element. In the game, players can move their pieces to earn money and then use that money to build new buildings, upgrade their houses, and much more. The ultimate goal is to drive other players into bankruptcy by acquiring all pieces of property, essentially creating a “monopoly.”

Monopoly GO: Comic Crunch Rewards and Milestones

Comic Crunch Monopoly GO is loaded with Finale Partner tokens, dice rolls, sticker packs, and more. Here's every milestone and reward.

By Umama Ali

In Monopoly GO , players move according to the number of dice they get, and the game proceeds with renting, trading, and buying properties. If players have finished their dice rolls and want to get some more, here’s how they can do it.

Updated by Umama Ali on July 24, 2026: Without dice, you can’t roll around the board, build landmarks, or participate in any tournaments. Running out of dice can slow down your progress in Monopoly GO, leaving you at a disadvantage compared to other players. With the release of Finale Partners, fans are looking for more dice rolls. We’ve updated this guide with a bunch of new links that offer free dice rolls so that you can keep building in Monopoly GO. Check back regularly to find new Monopoly GO dice links.

I found only one new dice link on July 24 . You can find all the active Monopoly GO dice links in the table below.

How to Redeem Dice Links in Monopoly GO

To redeem these links, tycoons can follow these simple steps:

  • Open a link on your phone. This will launch the Monopoly GO app on your device.
  • All you need to do then is click 'Collect,' and you'll get dice rolls for free. They will be automatically added to your account.

How To Get Free Dice Rolls In Monopoly Go

Login Daily

Like most mobile games nowadays, Monopoly GO also offers incentives for players so that they frequently play the game. One of the daily treats is free dice rolls, so logging in daily is one way to get them. In addition to dice rolls, players have the chance to win other exciting prizes as well.

Free Gifts

Fans can also grab free gifts every eight hours . For this, you will need to head over to the in-game store and keep swiping until you see the gift icon. Click on it, and you’ll get a handful of dice rolls for free.

Along with dice, these gifts can also include things like minigame tokens, which always come in handy during events. Since the gift refreshes every eight hours, fans can check in a few times each day to keep collecting them.

Invite Friends

Monopoly GO offers generous rewards for players who successfully invite others to join the game. If a player invites a friend, and the invited friend joins the game, both of them get 30 extra rolls . Players can keep getting 30 free rolls for inviting up to 30 friends , given that they accept the invitation. And of course, the game is just more fun when you play with friends.

Collect Community Chest Rewards

Community chests are great because they offer a variety of rewards. Players can open these chests to earn money, and if they help a friend with a community chest, they can earn some free rolls.

To make the most out of the community chest, players must ensure that they have at least 9 active in-game friends.

Complete Sticker Albums

Players collect stickers throughout Monopoly GO , and they are not just a fun part of the game; they can help players get dice rolls , too. For every sticker set or album that players complete, they receive dice rolls.

While the free rolls earned through sticker albums are more than those obtained after completing a set, the process of completing an album can be more time-consuming. At the moment, the Monopoly Ever After sticker album is live in the game.

Monopoly GO: How to Play and Win the Partner Event

Partner Event is a popular social event in Monopoly GO that allows tycoons to team up with their friends. Here’s everything you need to know about it.

By Umama Ali

Participate in Events and Tournaments

If you want a bunch of dice rolls, consider participating in events and tournaments. The game introduces new events regularly, and by completing their milestones, you can claim dice rolls, different sticker packs, in-game money, and many other exciting prizes . Tournaments also pack a lot of stellar rewards, so players should aim to secure a high position on the tournament leaderboard to make the most of them.

Stay ahead in Monopoly GO — subscribe for curated dice links

By subscribing, you agree to receive newsletter and marketing emails, and accept our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. You can unsubscribe anytime.

Apart from solo events, Monopoly GO also has minigames like Partner events and Treasure Hunts that you can play to earn even more rewards. Partner events often offer Swap Packs and Wild Stickers, which can help you complete your sticker albums. Sometimes, you can also get cosmetics like shield skins and board tokens. In Partner Events and Tycoon Racers, you play with friends, while Treasure Hunts and Prize Drops are solo and can be played on your own.

Flash Events

Apart from the main events and tournaments, Monopoly GO also has a number of special events. From Mega Heist to Wheel Boost, the game offers many events to help you grab rewards like dice rolls. However, keep in mind that their timings change every day, so check the daily schedule and play the game while they are live to make the most of them.

Quick Wins

Quick Wins are basic tasks that you can complete to earn a variety of Monopoly GO items, like dice, cash, minigame tokens, and even sticker packs. These tasks usually involve things like landing on certain tiles, doing Shutdowns, or rolling the dice a set number of times.

item.title: Crimson Desert Releases Patch Notes for Update 1.15
item.description:
Pearl Abyss releases a brand-new update for Crimson Desert , though unlike recent updates, this one is largely interested in fixing issues and stabilizing the game for players. Since its launch, Crimson Desert has seen a major evolution driven largely by player behavior in-game and feedback provided to the developers. The result has been massive for the game, both in keeping players happy while attracting others through positive word of mouth.

Unfortunately, initial reviews of Crimson Desert proved to be more mixed than anticipated, resulting in a 30% drop in shares. However, Pearl Abyss focused on its players with rapid-fire updates to Crimson Desert , fixing issues, addressing frustrations, and adding new content. The result was a huge boost to the player base as well as the game rocketing past major sales milestones. While things may have settled a bit in recent months, Pearl Abyss continues to update the game, with plans for bigger content drops in the future.

Crimson Desert Studio Promises Continued Support As Long As There's Demand

Pearl Abyss discusses the constant updates Crimson Desert receives, promising to continue the support to help keep the player base high.

By Derek Nichols

While previous updates for Crimson Desert have typically added major new features and content, such as tweaking the control schemes or adding the popular Re-blockade endgame enhancement, the July 23 update is a bit smaller than what players have come to expect. Despite not containing new features to dig into, the patch itself is important for keeping things stable as it fixes numerous issues plaguing the experience for fans.

For players who enjoy some of the quieter moments of Crimson Desert , specifically the housing and farming aspects of the game, this patch fixes a couple of issues related to growing and harvesting crops. In addition, there was an issue that made large fish being transported on the player's back disappear when collecting other fish from a trap. Players using either Oongka or Damiane can also save their loadouts, as the issue that prevented the lock status of equipped gear from staying saved has finally been resolved.

The patch also addresses a bigger issue that has seemingly arisen from the recently added Cross Save feature for Crimson Desert . Originally added in patch 1.14, Cross Save allowed players to continue their journey through Pywel across PlayStation, Xbox, or PC through the same save data. However, it seems like some players were experiencing crashing-related issues specifically when attempting to load the data on a different platform. With this update, that bug has been fixed, meaning players can once again hop around various platforms.

For those looking for new content to dig into, they'll need to wait a bit longer. Even though patches tend to release each week, Pearl Abyss has bigger plans currently in the works as the developer teased major DLC coming to Crimson Desert . While the admission was light on details or even a timeframe of when to expect it, Director of marketing and PR, Will Powers, hinted that the upcoming project was specifically labeled as DLC and there's a good reason why the studio is taking that approach to it. With Gamescom right around the corner, some fans are hoping to see a glimpse at what Pearl Abyss has planned, but for now, players will need to wait a bit longer.

Crimson Desert Update 1.15 Patch Notes

Main Improvements

Content

  • Fixed an issue where certain bosses would appear transparent during battle.
  • Fixed an issue where crops would stop growing in certain situations.
  • Fixed an issue where crops could not be harvested in certain situations.
  • [Oongka/Damiane] Fixed an issue where the lock status of equipped gear would not be saved.
  • Fixed an issue where the player could not attack while riding the quest objective bear to the village, during the "Scattered Honey Jars" quest.
  • Changed the location of the "Mace of Ambition" so that it can be obtained more easily.
  • Fixed an issue where a large fish carried on the player’s back would disappear when collecting fish from a fish trap.

Controls

  • Fixed an issue where the crosshair for "Axiom Force" would appear even when the target was outside its activation range.
  • Fixed an issue where, in certain locations, the camera would remain zoomed in while swimming.

Combat / Action

  • Fixed an issue where the Wyvern could not be summoned while in midair.
  • Fixed an issue where "Aerial Roll" traveled an unusually short distance when used after "Aerial Maneuver."

Graphics / Settings

  • Fixed an issue where the colors and transparency of certain UI elements would appear abnormally when HDR was enabled.

Localization

  • Fixed various localization errors and improved localization quality across all languages.

Others

  • Fixed an issue where the game would occasionally crash when loading the cross-save data.
  • Fixed an issue where the character's posture would appear unnatural while riding a mount.
  • Fixed an issue where wagons would occasionally disappear when using the "Escape" function with stolen wagons.
  • Fixed an issue where Kliff would partially sink into the ground when using "Blinding Flash Finisher" on a slope.

item.title: New RPG on Steam is The Elder Scrolls Meets Elden Ring
item.description:
The open-world RPG genre has been dominated by massive adventures that let players step into dangerous fantasy worlds, create their own stories, and decide how they want to survive. From The Elder Scrolls giving players endless freedom to Elden Ring rewarding curiosity and exploration, there has always been an audience looking for games that make the journey itself the biggest part of the experience. Now, a new indie RPG on Steam is looking to capture that same feeling with a scaled-down version of games like The Elder Scrolls and Elden Ring .

Over the last few years, indie RPGs have started filling the gap as players wait years for The Elder Scrolls 6 or FromSoftware's next fantasy world (of course, that wait hasn't been as long as TES6 ). Games like Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon have shown that smaller studios can still create huge worlds where every nook and cranny is worth exploring. That same approach appears to be at the heart of AetherCycle , developed by Deep Interactive, as it packages grandiose worlds into a smaller, but no less dense package when it launches on Steam in November 2026.

Steam Officially Makes 6 Games 100% Free Until July 27, Available Right Now

Steam's Free Weekend promotion is officially live now, with PC gamers able to download and play six games completely free of charge until July 27.

1
By Joshua Duckworth

AetherCycle is 2026's Big Elder Scrolls-Like Game

Check Out AetherCycle on Steam

AetherCycle is a first-person action RPG that blends the freedom of The Elder Scrolls with the challenging combat philosophy of Elden Ring , while leaning closer in scale and structure to games like Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon . For those unfamiliar, Tainted Grail: Fall of Avalon was the biggest Elder Scrolls -like game of 2025, and AetherCycle could follow in its footsteps for 2026 (but not without bringing its own world to the table). In it, players will explore a vast world shaped by the mysterious Cycle, a force that changes the balance of danger and rewards across the land. The adventure focuses on discovering ancient ruins, uncovering hidden paths, battling powerful enemies, and building a character that fits each player's preferred playstyle.

AetherCycle Features at a Glance

  • First-person action combat: Fight enemies and bosses using weapons, abilities, and precise timing.
  • Open-world exploration: Discover ancient ruins, villages, underground areas, hidden paths, and forgotten locations.
  • The Cycle system: Experience a world that changes over time, shifting the balance between danger and reward.
  • Character progression: Level up your character, improve attributes, unlock abilities, and customize your build.
  • Loot-driven gear system: Collect weapons, armor, and items with randomized stats, rarity levels, and unique effects.
  • Solo and co-op multiplayer: Explore the world, complete quests, defeat bosses, and progress alongside friends.

​​​​​​​

Beyond its combat and progression systems, AetherCycle is also leaning heavily into the feeling of adventure. The world is filled with locations waiting to be discovered, from peaceful villages to dangerous underground domains hiding powerful enemies and valuable rewards. The Cycle itself adds another layer to exploration, as the open world is truly living, not completely static, and players will need to adapt as they continue their journey.

While AetherCycle is not trying to directly compete with the massive scale of The Elder Scrolls or the difficulty of Elden Ring , it is clearly targeting the same type of player who wants to get lost in a fantasy world and create their own path. How it is received ultimately remains to be seen, but the game is immediately one of the best options for an Elder Scrolls-like RPG when it does release in November 2026.

Upcoming Releases

item.title: Ranking Every Grand Theft Auto Game From Worst To Best
item.description:
Updated on July 24, 2026 by Mark Sammut: With GTA 6 slowly approaching, now is the time to revisit one of the many fantastic GTA games.

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto is the biggest open-world franchise of all time, and "open-world" might be unnecessary. Despite fairly humble origins, GTA blossomed into a cultural juggernaut once it went 3D and basically wrote the playbook for what a modern sandbox game should be. In a few months, GTA 6 becomes a reality, but it will need to be an all-time great to rank above the likes of San Andreas and GTA 5 .

Rockstar hasn't dropped a bad entry yet, but that doesn't mean every game is roughly of the same quality. In fact, a huge gap separates the best from the worst and the most mediocre, and everyone will have their own preferences. Still, let's try to answer the age-old question, "Which is the greatest GTA game ?"

One Of The Most Disastrous Rockstar Launches Of All Time

Fans were disappointed to the moon and back when Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition launched. The compilation was a lackluster effort to upscale the classic 3D games for the next generation and was lambasted by fans and critics alike. The titles were plagued with bugs and, because they were based on the mobile versions, looked worse than the original games. Even with all the patches that have addressed the many issues in this title, this cash grab is still probably Rockstar's biggest blemish when it comes to proper games.

5 Near-Perfect Open-World Crime Games Overshadowed By Grand Theft Auto

GTA 6 is poised to stand in a league of its own, but there was a time when the iconic open-world crime series had some really decent competitors.

By Vlad Mazanko

Rockstar released several updates to address its many issues, and modders also helped fix the PC iteration, so the trilogy is playable nowadays. However, GTA 3 , Vice City , and San Andreas deserve full-scale dedicated remasters, especially if they are going to essentially replace the original versions.

11 Grand Theft Auto

The Almost Unrecognizable Originator

Grand Theft Auto
Released
November 28, 1997

WHERE TO PLAY

PHYSICAL

Platform(s)
PC, PS1, Nintendo Game Boy Color
Genre(s)

The game that started it all had clunky controls, which made driving nearly impossible, but it had charm regardless. The ability to get into any car made Grand Theft Auto a hit and set the bedrock for this franchise to dominate the gaming industry in a few years' time. To this day, it's hard to believe this series became a reality because of a simple glitch that helped developers uncover a fun gameplay loop with a ton of potential.

Driving recklessly through intersections and colliding with other vehicles provided an exhilarating experience unlike anything out there, with players having to do everything in their power to avoid the cops in breakneck chases that still feel tense to this day. This top-down game laid the foundation for what would later become one of the best-selling video game franchises of all time.

Players who had a great time messing around in the original Grand Theft Auto will be glad to know that an expansion was released that let players roam around the streets of London in the late 60s. Most of Grand Theft Auto 's gameplay is left intact, with the change in setting being the most notable thing about this expansion.

Some people felt this expansion didn't do much to address the issues present in the original game, but players who loved its simple arcade-like gameplay will love what London 1969 has to offer. This expansion received a standalone release in the UK, which proved that many people enjoyed this unique addition to the legacy of the game that started it all.

The map is pretty much similar to the first one, making it easy to see why Rockstar didn't charge anything for this additional chapter.

Still, this shouldn't take away from the sheer fun players can enjoy as they wreak havoc in London once again. This expansion may not be a huge change from the norm, but it is worth checking out for fans of GTA 's fun gameplay, where players are encouraged to go bonkers and create as much chaos as possible.

One of the lesser-known Grand Theft Auto games follows a similar style to Grand Theft Auto and Grand Theft Auto 2 . Contrasting with the first two Grand Theft Auto games, Grand Theft Auto Advance has vehicle-based missions and is easier to play than the original games. Given how difficult these classic GTA games were, this was a welcome change for fans.

Smart gameplay, combined with vibrant graphics, keeps the game enjoyable. Grand Theft Auto Advance is a fun portable version of the classic GTA formula , and the only reason it's ranked the lowest on the list is its hardware limitations rather than the quality of the title itself.

9 Grand Theft Auto 2

A Fantastic Sequel, And A Clear Bridge Between GTA and GTA 3

Grand Theft Auto 2

Grand Theft Auto 2 was a notable step up from the first game, improving police chases, weapons, driving, locations, and the camera. Although it still maintained a top-down perspective, GTA 2 significantly overhauled its systems and even its technology, setting the stage for the rest of the franchise. Anyone looking to try a top-down GTA should start with this one .

8 Best Open-World Top-Down Games, Ranked

Whether it's about survival, raising chaos, or planning a strategy, top-down shooters are still quite fun!

By Mehrdad Khayyat

GTA 2 's biggest upgrades were the introduction of a Respect Meter, distinct rival gangs with territories, and a heavier emphasis on non-linear progression. Rockstar would further expand these concepts in sequels, making them foundational parts of the Grand Theft Auto experience. Anywhere City also feels closer to a genuine place, primarily thanks to way more competent AI that would actually do stuff rather than randomly walk.

Compared to everything that came after, GTA 2 's ceiling is way lower, and there's only so high we can rank the game. However, as far as top-down sandboxes are concerned, GTA 2 is still among the best of all time.

8 Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories

A Respectable Portable GTA Experience

Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories
Released
October 31, 2006

Powered by

Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel to Vice City that was released for the PSP (PlayStation Portable) and later for the PlayStation 2. One of the more forgotten GTA games, Vice City Stories is best described as "unessential," although that doesn't mean it isn't fun. Considering the limitations of the PSP, Rockstar pulled off a minor miracle by creating a proper 3D open-world game that translated the GTA formula surprisingly well; however, Vice City Stories is a mixed bag.

This is the Lance Vance Dance!

Before getting to the negatives, let's first highlight Vice City Stories ' crowning achievement: The Empire Building system. A mechanical leap at the time, this mechanic lets you attack rival gangs, claim turf, pick a business, and defend your territory. Admittedly, the concept is better than the grind-heavy execution, but it is still a massive positive. Vice City Stories also has surprisingly good hand-to-hand combat, at least by GTA standards.

On the negative side, the campaign has some of the hardest missions in the franchise, and they aren't a "fun" kind of hard. Vic Vance is a weird protagonist with a backstory that doesn't match the chaotic sandbox gameplay. Finally, it's an open-world PSP game... the performance isn't great. The PS2 version sounds better, but Vice City Stories is far less impressive on the big screen.

7 Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

The Superior GTA Prequel On The PSP

Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories
Released
October 25, 2005

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Rockstar Leeds, Rockstar North
Platform(s)
Android, iOS, PC, PS2, PS3, PS Vita, PSP
Genre(s)
Third-Person Shooter, Sandbox
Powered by

Before Vice City Stories , Rockstar dumped Liberty City Stories on the PSP, a pretty impressive technical feat at the time. Like its successor, this 2005 game can be difficult to really appreciate today, particularly if it is played on something other than a PSP. While it doesn't hold up compared to Vice City or San Andreas , Liberty City Stories feels like a step up from GTA 3 , adding things like motorbikes, free-aiming, and improved camera controls.

Focusing on the fall of Liberty's mafia families and the rise of the Triads and Forellis, Liberty City Stories provides quite a bit of context for GTA 3 , justifying a playthrough on its own. However, you need to sit through repetitive missions, an underwhelming protagonist, and uneven performance, all of which were easier to look past in 2005 than they are in 2026.

Chinatown Wars is the best Grand Theft Auto spin-off game. Created for the Nintendo DS and PSP, Chinatown Wars marries classic-era GTA with the more popular modern releases, providing a top-down open-world experience that comes really close to capturing the chaotic magic of mainline entries like GTA 4 . The change in perspective takes a while to get used to, but fans who love the GTA gameplay loop will get familiar with Chinatown Wars in no time.

7 Best Mobile Games Published By Rockstar, Ranked

While best known for their Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption series, Rockstar Games has also published a number of titles for mobile platforms.

By Eman Fatima

Chinatown Wars is played from a top-down perspective, providing an experience reminiscent of the first two Grand Theft Autos but more profound. Leaving a trail of destruction in the player's wake in Chinatown Wars is GTA lunacy at its finest. To this day, players find it hard to believe that this cathartic open-world action-adventure game ran on portable hardware despite how ambitious it was.

5 Grand Theft Auto 3

The Most Groundbreaking Grand Theft Auto Game

Grand Theft Auto 3
Released
October 23, 2001

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Developer(s)
Rockstar Games
Platform(s)
PS2, Xbox (Original), PC, macOS, Android, iOS
Genre(s)
Action, Adventure
Powered by

G rand Theft Auto' s first adventure in 3D was way ahead of its time, and it basically wrote the blueprint for modern open-world games. Now, like nearly every pioneer, GTA 3 was surpassed quickly by its successors, including Rockstar's own Vice City and San Andreas . Nowadays, Liberty City is not only tiny but also devoid of much life; however, we cannot analyze GTA 3 just from a 2026 lens. In 2001, no other PS2 game was as massive, ambitious, and jaw-dropping as this masterpiece, and its legacy far overshadows its longevity.

Welcome to Liberty City. Where it all began. – Rockstar

Should you play GTA 3 nowadays? Yes, but keep expectations realistic. Clause's entry in the Leone family makes for a pretty darn solid crime story, even if it might not be quite as iconic as some of the later entries. Despite its limitations, the sandbox is still fun to mess around in. That said, if you don't enjoy GTA 3 , that doesn't mean you should skip Rockstar's other PS2 GTA games.

4 Grand Theft Auto: Vice City

The True Originator Of The Modern Day GTA

Grand Theft Auto: Vice City
Released
October 29, 2002

WHERE TO PLAY

DIGITAL

Developer(s)
Rockstar Games
Platform(s)
PS2, Xbox (Original), PC, iOS, Android, macOS
Genre(s)
Action, Adventure
Powered by

In Grand Theft Auto: Vice City , players rise from rags to riches as Tommy Vercetti. Including an airport, marinas, and a taxi cab company, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City captures the essence of Miami. The ability to purchase companies that generate money gave the game more replayability.

One feature that makes Grand Theft Auto: Vice City stand out is its shopping mall. An even more interactive shopping mall should be a part of the next Grand Theft Auto game. Whether players are doing pizza boy deliveries, taking the law into their own hands during its vigilante missions, or searching the locale for stunt jumps, there is plenty of content to keep players busy in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

3 Grand Theft Auto 5

The Most Successful Game Of All Time, And The Biggest GTA Game (So Far)

Grand Theft Auto 5
9 /10
Released
September 17, 2013

WHERE TO PLAY

SUBSCRIPTION
DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Developer(s)
Rockstar North
Platform(s)
Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One, Xbox 360, PC, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5
Genre(s)
Open-World, Action
Powered by

Well, here it is, the biggest entry in the franchise so far. Rockstar has been living off GTA 5 and GTA Online for more than a decade, releasing the base game across three console generations. Frustratingly, the single-player portion never received an expansion as the focus went entirely into the online mode; fortunately, the base content is more than great enough to hold its own.

Surviving is winning, Franklin. – Michael

Switching to a three-protagonist system, GTA 5 lets you swap between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor at nearly any time, which helps cut the tedious downtime between the actual fun bits. The campaign's biggest missions revolve around heists, requiring crew recruitment, setup plans, and choices, and these generally deliver fantastic set pieces that are worth the price of admission on their own. Although the combat and driving could still use a bit of work, they are far ahead of anything else in the franchise.

GTA Online

Grand Theft Auto Online
Released
October 1, 2013

WHERE TO PLAY

SUBSCRIPTION
DIGITAL
PHYSICAL

Developer(s)
Rockstar North
Platform(s)
PS5, PS4, PS3, Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One, Xbox 360, PC
Genre(s)
Open-World, Action
Powered by

There's a reason episodic DLCs didn't make the cut for Grand Theft Auto 5 , despite many reports stating that Rockstar planned to pursue this course of action. The rampant success of GTA Online pushed Rockstar to devote all its resources to make this game mode as perfect as possible, with players loving the idea of exploring this massive world with their friends and allowing players to live out a virtual life that is laden with crime off the wazoo.

Players can engage in heists, race around, and just kill players without a care in the world if they wish. There's something infinitely enjoyable about this game mode, making it clear why Grand Theft Auto 5 has been released on three separate console generations — the online component is that popular and continues to draw in numerous fans to this day.
